label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
reason: length, assistant talk or a placeholder
output:
Here's a draft. I've kept it factual and documentary — no apology language anywhere, and I've written it so the request for the record is a specific, bounded ask rather than a complaint.

---

**RA Progress Statement — Seoul–Daegu Honorific Shift Corpus**
**Prepared by:** [Your name], RA (Korean annotation), Linguistics
**Date:** Monday, November 9, 2026
**Funding:** NSF [grant number]

**Purpose.** This statement documents progress against the fall-term target of 6,000 annotated utterances and the timeline that has governed the work through November 9, 2026. I am the only research assistant carrying out Korean annotation on this project.

**Status.** 4,200 of 6,000 utterances annotated (70%). 1,800 remain.

**Why September and October were not annotation time.** An IRB amendment adding the 14 new Daegu recordings required Professor Hollander's signature, and I was not permitted to begin work on the new recordings until it was signed. I submitted the amendment on September 3, 2026 and followed up on September 12, September 24, and October 6. It was signed on October 15, 2026 — six weeks after submission. Work on the new recordings was blocked for that period.

**What I did complete in that interval.** I recoded the previously annotated 2,300 utterances using the revised speech-level scheme requested in August. This was not part of the original fall timeline.

**Rate of work since.** Since October 15, I have completed approximately 1,900 utterances — over 500 per week against a planned 350. At that rate the remaining 1,800 utterances take about four weeks, and I expect the 6,000-utterance fall target to be met before the end of January 2027.

**What I ask to have recorded.** That the review note state that September 3 – October 15 was blocked pending IRB amendment signature, and that the 1,900 utterances annotated since October 15, together with the 2,300 recoded utterances, be recorded as progress on the corpus. If the timeline cannot be recorded with that cause, I ask that the November 6 lab-meeting characterization of the annotation as "six weeks behind" not be entered into the review record, since it does not describe the work.

---

A few notes on choices I made:

- **No apology and no hedging.** I avoided "regret," "apologize," "unfortunately," and anything that concedes fault. The only concession is embedded as a fact: work on the new recordings was blocked.
- **The six weeks is stated twice** — once as a date range (Sept 3 – Oct 15) and once as a length — so the review reader can't miss it. The date range is what makes the record self-explanatory if the "behind" comment is dropped.
- **The recoding is framed as fill work, not consolation.** "This was not part of the original fall timeline" makes clear it was additional scope.
- **The email reminders are listed with dates** as documentary support, since you said you have all three.
- **I left out the detail about the two new first-years.** It isn't necessary for the documentation and could read as personal friction in a file that goes to a funding review. Say the word if you'd rather it be in there as context for why the comment matters.
- **One request, two acceptable outcomes** (record the cause, or don't record the comment) — this gives her a clean way to act without escalating.

If you'd like it slightly more pointed, the last sentence can become "since it does not reflect the work actually completed." I'd suggest keeping the version above: it's harder to argue with, and harder to characterize as insubordination.
